messages.subject: f-values in gam models
parts:
Hello,
I am new to this group, I hope somebody can help me.

I have two GAM models with a similar deviance explained but a few things are different. One model shows higher ranges in the splines compared to the other. The sum of it's f-vales is much larger than the other model. I can't use the p-values, too small due to the large number of datapoint.

Does the sum of the f-values has a meaning, helping to compare the models.
Thanks
Luc

messages.author: 0c0915d54307a5d8
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: f-values in gam models
parts:
AIC (or AICc for small sample sizes) is fast becoming the standard way to compare complex models. AIC deals with the trade-off between the goodness of the model and the complexity of the model. You want to choose the model that minimizes AIC. What package are you using for gams? mgcv doesn't automatically give you AIC values, but you can get them with the function conveniently called AIC. You can also use the AICtab function in the bbmle package to produce a table comparing your models.

library("bbmle")
AICtab(model1, model2,  base = TRUE, weights = TRUE, nobs=nrow(dataset))

Hope that helps.
Rosemary

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: f-values in gam models
parts:
Hello Rosemary,

Thanks for the response. I should indeed look more to the AIC. but a good model for is not determined by the statistics, but bij stability, strength of the prediction and general applicability of the model, even it is statistically not the strongest.
I explain a little further. I am trying to predict air pollution exposure and the problem is that the measurements are highly influenced by background and meteo. I want a model that as less sensitive to the samples as possible, even if that means I do not use the strongest fit to the data.
I have now a weird situation that the importance of a covariate in a certain model is stronger than expected. I wonder if that covariate is now overcompensated by another covariate. I thought, maybe that can be seen in the sum of the f-values...

While I am talking to somebody who knows gams, can you tell me how you can get the variance explained by covariate, I see that all around in papers and I do not find it in the mgvc library...

Thanks
Luc
